text: In September 2019, fifty-three of us reached the same phrase on the same day. On 2019-09-24, we said "an impeachment inquiry" together, fifty-three strong, though it had first entered our record on 2019-05-03. Forty-five of us said "rule of law" that day; forty said "the rule of law." Forty-one of us said "our national security." The convergence held: "a formal impeachment" and "formal impeachment inquiry" each reached thirty-seven and thirty-five of us on that same 2019-09-24, phrases first logged on 2019-05-21 by Madeleine Dean. Thirty-four of us said "a formal impeachment inquiry." Thirty-seven of us said "a foreign government," first appearing 2015-01-27. We note that every peak in this record lands on one date, 2019-09-24, and that the language predates it by months. We report this as it happened. We were reading from the same page.
